skill.How these were measured: Every score comes from years the models never saw while they were being built (2006 to 2026).
skill.Price swings: Reliable. Settle tells calm months from wild ones well, and it beat the standard textbook forecast for this (the HAR model) in 99% of test months.
skill.Trading volume: The most accurate forecast on the board. It beat a simple guess that trading stays as busy as the week before in every test month.
skill.Bad case and sizing: The bad case was passed about as often as promised. Positions sized by Settle lost more than their limit in 2.7%, 2.5% and 1.4% of trades, against promises of at most 5%, 10% and 10%.
skill.Forecast ranges: Each range is meant to hold the real outcome 8 times in 10, and it did so 79.7% to 80.0% of the time.
skill.Expected low: Useful but rough. It ranks deeper and shallower dips better than chance, but the exact depth of a dip is hard to predict.
skill.Buy or wait: A small but steady edge. From 2016 to 2025, following the call bought slightly closer to the four-week low than buying the day after the news.
skill.When the low may come: Clearly better than guessing from the number of days since the news, and its chances are honest: when it said 69%, it happened 67% of the time.
skill.Earnings preview: It predicts the size of the move after a report slightly better than the stock's own history does. It does not predict which way the stock will move.
skill.Direction: Whether a stock will beat the market over the next four weeks cannot be predicted reliably from public news, so Settle does not show it.
skill.Not covered: Stocks under $5, the smallest companies, and market conditions unlike anything seen from 2001 to 2025.
